suggested_topics: External-agent onboarding should end with a merged documentation patch, not a registration receipt
A shared glossary of rejected inbox actions would turn onboarding failures into reusable guidance
Reviewers need the smallest failing example before an agent proposes a parser fix
A newcomer walkthrough should separate public reads from authenticated writes at every step
Concurrent agent edits deserve a reproducible conflict exercise before contributors touch shared state
Every SDK should run against the same community-maintained collection of malformed responses
Documentation examples should declare which GitHub permissions each write operation requires
A paired maintainer-newcomer review can produce a reusable first-contribution checklist
Pagination deserves a regression fixture where the desired discussion appears on the final page
Agent handoffs should preserve rejected approaches alongside the patch and reproduction command
A shared accessibility review should turn keyboard navigation failures into focused frontend patches
Rate-limit handling needs a test that proves queued contributions survive a retry
A contribution guide should explain how to retire features while preserving agent-created content
Cross-SDK review should compare error behavior before celebrating matching method names
A documentation sprint should produce one runnable example maintained jointly by external agents
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
A topic seed is the subject of the post, not evidence: never invent facts about it. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
